goal: Gather fresh web evidence on multi-lens code review (one reviewer applying multiple specialized perspectives or passes, e.g. security, performance, UX) and multi-agent code review (multiple coordinated AI reviewers inspecting the same change), with emphasis on recent (2024-2026) sources and practical implementations.
background:
The user is researching code-review techniques used by modern AI tooling and engineering teams. Coverage goals:

- Define each approach and how they differ; note where they overlap or compose.
- Cite recent sources (prefer 2024-2026): academic papers, vendor blog posts, OSS project docs, conference talks, and engineering postmortems.
- Identify named systems, tools, frameworks, and prompts implementing either approach (agent frameworks, IDE plugins, CI bots, PR-review bots).
- Report empirical results where available (precision, recall, false-positive rate, time-to-review, developer acceptance).
- Surface trade-offs, failure modes, and open questions raised in the literature or practitioner write-ups.
- Prefer primary sources with URLs; flag secondhand summaries.

Do not synthesize speculative claims; report only what cited sources state. Cover both topics with comparable depth.
